sentences.text: Ctenurella is a member of the class Placodermi, belonging to the family Ptyctodontidae.
This small placoderm reached a length of just 13 cm and possessed reduced armor consisting of only a few thin plates on its head and shoulder region.
It featured two dorsal fins and a rear body section that was relatively long and low.
Male Ctenurella possessed hook-shaped sex organs known as claspers.
Unlike most relatives that likely fed on the ocean floor, Ctenurella's well-developed fins suggest it probably also swam in open waters.
The first fossils of Ctenurella were discovered in the Strunde valley within the Paffrather Kalkmulde.
A 1997 description by Long revealed that the original restoration of Ctenurella gladbachensis incorrectly showed the skull-roof bones meeting behind the nuchal plate.
In 1997, Long split the species Ctenurella gardineri into the new genus Austroptyctodus, restricting the genus Ctenurella to sites in Germany.
Ctenurella lived during the Givetian to Frasnian stages, between 383.4 and 379 million years ago.
Researchers think that the analogous features found in unrelated living chimaeras and ptyctodonts like Ctenurella represent an example of convergent evolution.
